ai.literal: Virtue he does not speak, non-virtuous things even if he does, a person, behind one's back he does not speak, to say is sweet.
ai.translation: Even if a person does not speak of virtue and commits acts of vice, it is still a redeeming good if it can be said of him, 'he does not speak ill of others behind their backs.'
ai.modern: ஒருவன் அறவழிகளைப் பேசாமல், பாவங்களையே செய்தாலும் கூட, அவன் 'பிறரைப் புறங்கூற மாட்டான்' என்று பிறர் சொல்வது அவனுக்கு நன்மையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme gravity of backbiting by comparing it with other vices. Even if a person fails to speak of virtuous things and actively commits sinful deeds, there is still a saving grace if others can say of him that he never speaks ill of anyone behind their back. The word 'இனிது' (sweet or good) indicates that avoiding backbiting is so valuable that it brings a redeeming goodness to an otherwise flawed character. The poet emphasizes that backbiting is a vice so destructive that abstaining from it is a great virtue in itself.

ai.literal: Than destroying virtue and doing evil deeds, it is indeed worse to ruin someone behind their back and smile falsely.
ai.translation: Worse than destroying virtue and committing evil deeds is slandering someone behind their back and then smiling falsely to their face.
ai.modern: அறத்தை அழித்துத் தீமைகளைச் செய்வதை விட, ஒருவரைப் பின்னால் பழித்துப் பேசிவிட்டு நேரில் பொய்மையாகச் சிரிப்பது மிகவும் தீமையானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme deceitfulness of backbiting. The author compares two wrongs: destroying virtue to commit evil deeds, and slandering someone behind their back while pretending to be friendly to their face. The latter is declared to be far worse. The words 'புறன் அழீஇ' (ruining behind the back) and 'பொய்த்து நகை' (smiling falsely) vividly depict the hypocrisy of a backbiter, showing that betrayal of trust is more damaging than open vice.

ai.literal: Than living a life of backbiting and lying, dying will, even by the decree of virtue, give benefit.
ai.translation: Dying is far better than living a life of deceit and backbiting; even the god of death will deem such a death as a virtue that brings benefit.
ai.modern: புறம்பேசிப் பொய் சொல்லி உயிர் வாழ்வதை விடச் சாதல் சிறந்தது; அது அறநெறிப்படியும் நன்மையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the extreme dishonor of backbiting and deceitful living. The author states that it is much better to die than to sustain one's life through slander and lies. Even the god of death, who acts as the arbiter of virtue, will consider such a death as a beneficial and righteous choice rather than a sinful life. The key words 'புறங்கூறி' (backbiting) and 'பொய்த்து' (lying) represent the vices, while 'சாதல்' (dying) is presented as a superior alternative that brings 'ஆக்கம்' (benefit/goodness).

words.gloss: not looking behind (not considering the consequences)

ai.literal: Standing in front, even if speaking without kindness, do not speak, standing in front, the word that does not look behind.
ai.translation: Even if you speak ruthlessly to someone's face, do not speak words in their absence that you cannot stand by when you face them later.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய நேருக்கு நேர் நின்று இரக்கமில்லாமல் பேசினாலும் பேசலாம்; ஆனால் அவர் இல்லாதபோது, பின்னர் அவரே நேரில் வந்து நிற்கும் போது எதிர்கொள்ள முடியாத சொற்களைப் புறங்கூறிப் பேசக்கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts direct, harsh criticism with backbiting. The poet states that it is acceptable to stand directly in front of someone and speak words completely devoid of kindness. However, one must never speak words behind their back that they cannot stand by or face up to when they meet them in person later. The key contrast is between the courage of direct, albeit harsh, confrontation and the cowardice of backbiting which cannot bear the light of a face-to-face meeting.

ai.literal: The state of not having a heart that speaks virtue will be seen by the meanness of speaking behind others' backs.
ai.translation: That a person does not truly possess a heart that speaks of virtue will be revealed by the meanness of their backbiting.
ai.modern: அறத்தைப் பேசுகின்ற நெஞ்சத்தை உடையவனாக ஒருவன் இல்லாத தன்மை, அவன் பிறரைப் பற்றிப் புறங்கூறும் இழிவான செயலால் அறியப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet exposes the hypocrisy of those who speak of virtue but slander others in secret. Even if a person outwardly preaches righteousness, their lack of a truly virtuous heart (அன்மை) is clearly revealed by the meanness (புன்மை) of their backbiting. The poet shows that one's private speech behind others' backs is the true test of their inner character.

ai.literal: Another's fault he who speaks, his own faults even among, the most hurtful kind having selected, to be spoken will be.
ai.translation: He who speaks of another's faults will have his own faults searched out and spoken of, especially those that are most hurtful.
ai.modern: பிறருடைய குற்றங்களைப் பற்றிப் புறங்கூறிப் பேசுபவனுடைய சொந்தக் குற்றங்களுக்குள்ளும் மிகக் கொடிய குற்றங்களைத் தேடித் தேர்ந்தெடுத்துப் பிறரால் பேசப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the consequences of backbiting and exposing the flaws of others. If a person gossips about another's faults, society will retaliate by exposing their own flaws. Crucially, people will not just speak of any minor flaw; they will search out and select (தெரிந்து) the most sensitive, hurtful, and damaging secrets (திறன்) to expose. Thus, speaking ill of others ultimately invites the most painful exposure of one's own character.

words.gloss: those who do not know how

ai.literal: Dividingly speaking, friends they will separate, pleasantly speaking, friendship cultivating, those who do not know how.
ai.translation: Those who do not know how to cultivate friendship by speaking pleasantly will speak divisively and alienate even their own friends.
ai.modern: இனிமையாகப் பேசி நட்பை வளர்க்கத் தெரியாதவர்கள், பிரிவினை உண்டாக்கும்படிப் பேசித் தம் நண்பர்களையும் பிரித்துவிடுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two ways of speaking and their effects on relationships. Those who do not know how to nurture friendships by speaking pleasantly and joyfully (நகச்சொல்லி) end up doing the opposite. By speaking behind people's backs or carrying tales, they create discord (பகச்சொல்லி) and alienate even their closest companions (கேளிர்). The poet highlights that the inability to speak kindly and constructively inevitably leads to the destruction of one's own social circle.

ai.literal: Those who have the habit of proclaiming even the faults of those who are close, what indeed will they do towards strangers?
ai.translation: What indeed will those who make a habit of broadcasting even the faults of their close friends do when it comes to strangers?
ai.modern: நெருங்கிய நண்பர்களின் குற்றங்களையும் பிறரிடம் தூற்றிப் பேசும் இயல்புடையவர்கள், தமக்குத் தொடர்பில்லாத அந்நியர்களிடம் என்னதான் செய்யமாட்டார்கள்?
ai.explanation: This couplet exposes the character of those who indulge in backbiting. If a person has the habit of broadcasting the faults of their own close associates ('துன்னியார்'), they will certainly not hesitate to slander strangers ('ஏதிலார்'). The rhetorical question 'what indeed will they do' ('என்னை கொல்') emphasizes that their capacity for malice towards outsiders is boundless. The word 'தூற்றும்' literally means to scatter or winnow, vividly illustrating how gossip-mongers spread the secrets of others far and wide.

ai.literal: Virtue considering, bears indeed the earth, behind-the-back watching-for, mean words of-one-who-speaks the-burden.
ai.translation: Does the earth bear the heavy burden of one who watches for another's absence to speak mean words, only because she considers it her virtue to endure?
ai.modern: அறத்தைக் கருதித்தான் இந்த பூமி, பிறர் இல்லாத சமயம் பார்த்துப் புறங்கூறிப் பேசுகின்றவனுடைய உடலாகிய பாரத்தைச் சுமக்கிறதோ?
ai.explanation: The poet wonders why the earth continues to bear the weight of a person who slanders others behind their back. He suggests that the earth does not do this out of any respect for the slanderer, but solely because she considers it her own virtue to endure all burdens patiently. The word 'வையம்' (earth) is personified as a patient mother, and 'அறன் நோக்கி' (considering virtue) explains her motivation. This highlights how despicable backbiting is, as even the earth finds the slanderer to be an unbearable burden, carrying them only out of a sense of duty.

words.gloss: if they are able to see

ai.literal: If they are able to see their own fault like strangers' fault, is there evil to the enduring soul?
ai.translation: If people could look at their own faults in the same way they look at the faults of strangers, is there any harm that can ever come to their enduring lives?
ai.modern: அயலாரின் குற்றத்தைக் காண்பது போலத் தம்முடைய குற்றத்தையும் காண வல்லவரானால், நிலைபெற்று வாழும் உயிர்க்கு ஏதேனும் துன்பம் உண்டோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet addresses the human tendency to judge others while ignoring one's own flaws. The poet suggests that if we could examine our own faults with the same critical eye we use for strangers, we would naturally correct ourselves. By focusing on self-improvement rather than backbiting, we protect ourselves from harm. Consequently, no evil can ever affect a life that is guided by such self-awareness.
